senses.gloss: (b. h. תֵּבָה; Egyptian; v., however, תָּבָא)ship, ark, chest.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 31">Gen. R. s. 31</cite> (play on <he>קנים</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 6:14">Gen. VI, 14</cite>) <he>מה הקן … אף תֵּיבָתְךָ וכ׳</he> as birds (v. <cite ref="S01505"><he>קֵן</he></cite>) make the leper clean, so does thy ark cleanse thee.
Ib. על שם תֵּיבָתוֹ של נח (it is called t’biḳin) from the measures of Noah’s ark.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 5:1:17">Y. Erub. V, 22ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>כיצד היו ישראל … כת׳</he> how did the Israelites march in the desert?… like a chest (forming a square), opp. <he>כקורה</he> like a beam (in columns).

<cite ref="Menachot 94b:1">Men. 94ᵇ</cite> <he>כמין ת׳ פרוצה</he> (the shape of the show-bread was) that of an open chest (without a lid and with a level bottom), opp. <he>כמין ספינה רוקדת</he> like a rocking ship (with a curved bottom). Sifra M’tsorʿa, Zab., Par. 1, ch. II <he>תֵּיבַת הבלנים</he> the bathers’ chest.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 10:1">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. X, 1</cite>, sq.; a. fr.—Pl. <he>תֵּבוֹת</he>, <cite ref="V00516"><he>תֵּי׳</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 1:10">Midr. Till. to Ps. I</cite> <he>היה צריך לעשות ת׳ הרבה</he> he would have been obliged to build many arks.
Y. Sot. VIII, beg. 22ᵇ שהיו עשויין ת׳ ת׳ they (the Egyptians) were arrayed in squares.—Esp. the chest in the synagogue containing the scrolls of the Pentateuch.
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 2:1">Taan. II, 1</cite> <he>מוציאין את הת׳ וכ׳</he> (at prayer meetings) they bring the chest out to the open place of the town, and put ashes of wood on the chest &c.

Meg. III, 1 בני העיר … בה״כ לוקחין ת׳ ת׳ וכ׳ if the citizens of a township sell … a synagogue, they may buy (for the money) a book chest; if they sell a chest, they may buy book wrappers; a. fr.—עבר לפני הת׳, ירד לפני הת׳ to go before the chest, to act as reader of prayers.
<cite ref="Berakhot 34a:11">Ber. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>שירד לפני הת׳ וכ׳</he> who recited the prayers in the presence of &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 5:3">Ib. V, 3</cite> <he>העובר לפני הת׳ וטעה וכ׳</he> if a reader makes a mistake (reads heretical formulas), another person must pass before the chest in his place.
<cite ref="Berakhot 34a:4">Ib. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>העובר לפני הת׳ צריך לסרב</he> he that is asked to read the prayers &c., v. <cite ref="O01511"><he>סָרַב</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 2:2">Taan. II, 2</cite> <he>מורידין לפני הת׳ וכ׳</he> we depute as reader (on fast days) an old man &c.; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Menachot 30b:1">Men. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ בת שתי וכ׳</he> a word of two letters.

<cite ref="Shabbat 104a:2">Sabb. 104ᵃ</cite> they did not know <he>הי באמצע ת׳ וכ׳</he> in which (of the two forms of the letters <cite ref="M01810"><he>מנצפ״ך</he></cite>) were to be employed in the middle of a word, and which at the end; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="V00411"><he>תֵּיבוֹת</he></cite>, <he>תֵּיבִיּוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Chullin 64b:7">Ḥull. 64ᵇ</cite> <he>דפסק … ת׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 40) where the scribe divides them into two words; <cite ref="Chullin 65a:1">ib. 65ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:9">Y. Meg. I, 71ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>תיביות</he>; a. e.
